title: Odd jobs, selling papers and losing his legs on a streetcar
summary: White says he never held regular work, farmed brick, sold newspapers and then jumped a car, which cost him his legs.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: So let's see, uh, when World War, during World War I, were you a grown man then?
You were, you were already out working and everything, aren't you?

No, I never did work. I always did. I never did work because I had old people, or used to have, they had their own, you understand, was, was well, well, uh, well-doers, you understand. All I used to do, when they used to, I used to get money from them if I wanted anything. But I used to work, though. Like I used to, them time I used to farm brick, go sell 15 cents a bucket, or mop, or do, you know, different little job, till I make enough money. I used to make enough money to keep me going, you understand. Uh-huh. And after, then after I pulled around, I went, pulled around, I went, pulled around, selling paper. After I got through selling paper, when I wasn't satisfied to sell paper, I went and jumped on the car. See, when I jumped on the car, that way I got my legs taken off. But outside of that ship, I was all right then, man.

Yeah, I was selling newspaper. I was selling newspaper right there for Cora, on the next street. I was selling paper for Cora, for Ms. Cora. And all those, and then the place around here, you can call. They don't know me. White, colored, all.
